L3: cobs_encoder_write checks byte==0 before the full-group (0xff) flush and flushes only after storing, whereas the oracle flushes the full group first and treats 0x00 as a boundary; the encoded length mismatches at the 254-char/full-group boundary (test_encode/test_encode_stream).
Uses (val>>4)^table[val&0x0f] instead of the oracle's (val<<4)^table[val>>4] (low nibble + right shift vs high nibble + left shift), so crc8_ccitt mismatches (expected 0xF3).

Decodes the length but adds 'if (*len > FCB_MAX_LEN) return -EINVAL' before writing *len; an erased 0xff pattern decodes to ~0x7fff, trips the guard and fails fcb_tc_pretest, while the oracle has no such limit (and a special -ENOTSUP for double-erased).

fcb_walk rewritten to loop 'while (fcb_getnext_nolock(...) == 0)' holding the mutex across the callback and returning 0 always, dropping the -ENOTSUP stop, per-item unlock and sector-boundary early return of the oracle; element counts read by the callback are wrong (append_fill).

k_p4wq_submit drops item->deadline += k_cycle_get_32() (delta-to-absolute), the done_sem init and the ahead-items early return, replacing wake logic with a manual lowest-item scan; without the absolute deadline the rb/queue ordering is wrong and the run crashes.
modem_chat_script_init memsets the script but drops the oracle's 'script->name = ""' sentinel, leaving name NULL for later use -> crash.
modem_pipe_notify_opened sets both event bits but only calls the OPENED callback, omitting the oracle's MODEM_PIPE_EVENT_TRANSMIT_IDLE callback, so test state lacks the TRANSMIT_IDLE bit.

modem_ubx_init assigns the whole ubx->unsol_matches = config->unsol_matches (struct-with-array copy) instead of copying .array/.size separately; 'incompatible types when assigning to struct' at modem_ubx.c:236.

osEventFlagsSet posts all flags via k_event_post(flags) and returns its result, whereas the oracle first reads already-set bits (k_event_test) and only posts/masks flags & ~rv; concurrent/basic event-flags tests fail because already-set bits are mishandled and the return value is wrong.

osThreadCreate deviates from the oracle in several ways: it omits the pre-create k_thread_custom_data_set(thread_def) (v1 signal wait/set resolve thread_def via k_thread custom_data, which the kernel initializes to NULL at thread create), passes a full K_THREAD_STACK_LEN(MAX) stack size regardless of thread_def->stacksize, and drops the priority/stacksize range asserts. The K_THREAD_STACK_LEN-is-element-count hypothesis is ruled out (k_thread_stack_t is 1 byte, so LEN returns aligned bytes); the most likely crash trigger is a NULL/racy custom_data in test_signal_events_isr, but the exact single line needs a debugger to confirm.
pm_device_runtime_enable lacks the oracle's lazy init 'if (pm->dev == NULL) { pm->dev = dev; ... }', so pm->dev stays NULL and later PM operations dereference it -> segfault.
spsc_pbuf_free drops the oracle's PADDING_MARK / next-packet-padding handling and unconditional wrap logic, breaking 0cpy corner tests.

spsc_pbuf_write drops the top-level 'len >= SPSC_PBUF_MAX_LEN -> -EINVAL' check and returns -ENOMEM for a short allocation, so oversized-length tests that expect -EINVAL fail (rlen not equal to -EINVAL).
stream_flash_progress_clear logs with a malformed string literal (stray double quotes around %s: ...for "%s"), producing 's undeclared' / 'expected )' syntax errors.
sys_multi_mem_blocks_alloc drops the count==0 branch (setting *blk_size=0) and the count>num_blocks precheck, and sets *blk_size from the allocator before checking count; multi alloc tests fail.
usbd_register_all_classes calls is_blocklisted(c_nd, blocklist) without the oracle's 'blocklist != NULL' guard, so a NULL blocklist is dereferenced -> segfault.

usbh_desc_get_next_function rewrites skipping to only look for the next IAD/interface (alternate 0), dropping the oracle's association bInterfaceCount skip logic and NULL/type semantics; descriptor walk test fails.

usbh_req_setup always allocates the control transfer on USB_CONTROL_EP_OUT (0x00) instead of selecting the endpoint based on request direction (usb_reqtype_is_to_device ? 0x00 : 0x80). This breaks IN-direction control requests needed during device enumeration (e.g. reading the device descriptor), causing 'HS device has wrong bMaxPacketSize0 8' and 'Failed to init new USB device'. Consequently udev stays NULL and all subsequent control tests fail; the later segfault is a downstream effect of the corrupted state.
z_log_msg_commit omits msg->hdr.timestamp = timestamp_func() before msg_commit, leaving the timestamp uninitialized; log processing on the garbage timestamp crashes.

zbus_chan_add_obs passes timeout (k_timeout_t) to _zbus_runtime_observer_node_alloc which expects a k_timepoint_t (oracle converts via sys_timepoint_calc/sys_timepoint_timeout) -> type mismatch compile error.
zbus_chan_add_obs_with_node drops the oracle's 'if (node->chan != NULL) return -EBUSY' guard (and adds asserts), so reusing an already-linked node is accepted instead of rejected with -EBUSY.
device_supported_handles_get drops the Z_DEVICE_DEPS_ENDS stop (only stops on DEVICE_HANDLE_NULL), so the supporting-device count can be wrong; deps scan test fails.
ring_buf_is_empty calls ring_buf_size_get before it is declared/defined -> implicit declaration and conflicting-types errors in ring_buffer.h.
spsc_pbuf_capacity returns pb->common.len instead of len - sizeof(uint32_t) (header slot not reserved), capacity is 4 bytes too large.
timespec_equal normalizes ta/tb before comparing, whereas the oracle compares the raw tv_sec/tv_nsec; normalization changes the semantics the test expects (unequal/equal behavior differs).
timespec_from_timeout drops the K_FOREVER/K_NO_WAIT handling and only asserts relative timeouts, so an absolute/forever timeout trips the assert -> ZEPHYR FATAL ERROR.
zbus_obs_is_enabled turns the oracle's _ZBUS_ASSERTs into CHECKIF early returns of -EINVAL, changing NULL-argument behavior; a test expecting the assert/graceful path fails.
